Stainless Steel Grades.content: Stainless steel is classified into different grades based on its chemical composition and crystalline structure:

items: Austenitic (300 series): Includes grades like 304 and 316. Non-magnetic, highly formable, weldable, used in kitchenware, architecture.
Ferritic (400 series): Magnetic, chromium-based, used in automotive exhaust systems and appliances.
Martensitic (400 series): Known for hardness and strength, magnetic, heat-treatable, used in cutlery and surgical tools.
Duplex: Mixed microstructure, higher strength, resistance to stress corrosion cracking, used in offshore platforms and chemical plants.

Types of Alloy Steel.content: Alloy steel is a type of steel that is alloyed with a variety of elements, such as manganese, chromium, nickel, tungsten, vanadium, and silicon, to improve its properties. Depending on the alloying elements and their proportions, alloy steel can be classified into different types.

items: Low-Alloy Steel: Contains less than 5% of alloying elements. Used for enhanced strength and toughness in applications like pipes, fittings, and structural components.
High-Alloy Steel: Contains more than 5% of alloying elements, including stainless and tool steels for high corrosion resistance, heat resistance, or wear resistance.
Structural Alloy Steel: Engineered for construction and heavy machinery offering high strength, ductility, and weldability.
Tool Steel: Exceptional hardness, wear resistance, and ability to hold a sharp edge, used for cutting tools, dies, and molds.
